scenario: Math builtins on a negative, non-integer input per LEXP.3.2 — abs, floor, ceil, trunc, sign. v=-3.5 separates floor (-4, largest int ≤ x) from trunc (-3, toward zero) and ceil (-3); abs preserves the Float type so |−3.5| == 3.5 (a type-losing impl would truncate to 3 and not fire); sign yields -1. −3.5 and 3.5 are exact dyadic floats, so the comparisons are exact. Companion to LEXP.3.1 (positive integer-valued v=4.0). `abs` is global; the four roundings are `math` members, called qualified after `import math` ([LIMP.3.3.4]), where LEXP.3.1 imports them bare.
rules_ds:
import math

schema T scope logical:
    v: Float key

rule r_abs:
    T t where abs(t.v) == 3.5
->
    log critical "abs"

rule r_floor:
    T t where math.floor(t.v) == -4
->
    log critical "floor"

rule r_ceil:
    T t where math.ceil(t.v) == -3
->
    log critical "ceil"

rule r_trunc:
    T t where math.trunc(t.v) == -3
->
    log critical "trunc"

rule r_sign:
    T t where math.sign(t.v) == -1
->
    log critical "sign"
